governanceNotes: D1 batch 37 (2026-09-23): deferred. Duplicate-scope class screen recorded 2026-09-23: (i) the catalog carries distinct organ-specific identities for every member of this umbrella - esophageal-cancer (published, carrying cardiac-arrhythmia and cardiomyopathy edges), stomach-cancer (published, carrying the depressive-disorder edge), colorectal-cancer (published, carrying peripheral-neuropathy and fecal-incontinence edges), biliary-tract-cancer (draft with the malnutrition-residuals edge), plus liver-cancer, pancreatic-cancer, and small-intestine-cancer as separate backlog identities - so any edge authored from gastrointestinal-cancers would run a parallel pathway alongside the organ-specific edge for the same disease in the same patient (the batch-22 diabetes-mellitus, batch-27 eczema, and batch-33 female-reproductive-disorders class deferrals all enforce this ban); (ii) pooling failure - the umbrella spans squamous, adenocarcinoma, and neuroendocrine histologies across foregut, midgut, and hindgut organs with different etiologies (Helicobacter, reflux, Barrett's, IBD, and viral liver pathways), different treatments (surgery, chemoradiation, TKI, immunotherapy), and different outcome profiles, so no single causal mechanism or evidentiary profile could honestly represent a class edge (mechanism-representativeness guard); (iii) the strongest available target candidates are already or would be owned by members - depression via stomach-cancer, malnutrition via biliary-tract-cancer, cardiac toxicity via esophageal-cancer - confirming that the class adds no non-duplicative pathway today; (iv) GIST-like mesenchymal tumors and gastrointestinal stromal-tumors identity further complicate class membership (not carcinoma at all), which is a nosology problem for governance rather than an authoring decision. Reopening condition: a governance merge decision that retires the organ-specific identities into this umbrella, or an umbrella-specific pooled evidence base with organ adjustment.
